title: HOW MIO MET KON
subtitle: the night of the fox's wedding
source: Folk belief: kitsune no yomeiri (a sun-shower is a fox's wedding; humans must not watch or follow); kitsunebi fox lanterns; Inari fox messengers. Mio and Kon backstory is original to the series.

lines.say: [cheerful] Everyone asks me where I found a talking fox.
[softer] Honestly? He found me.
[storytelling] I was five. Every summer I stayed with my grandma, at her tiny shrine up in the mountains.
cap: Every summer I stayed with my {o:grandma},

lines.say: [fond] She made the best inari sushi in the whole world.
One afternoon, it started raining... but the sun was still out.
[whispering, imitating an old woman] Grandma said, sun rain means the foxes are getting married. Never, ever follow them.
[sly] In Japan, they call it the fox's wedding.
[sheepish] So obviously... I followed them.
[awed] There were lanterns floating through the trees. Foxes in wedding robes, under a big red umbrella.
[small, scared] And then they were gone. It was dark. I didn't know where I was.
cap: I didn't know where I was.

lines.say: [tender] I just sat down and cried. And when I looked up... there was a little white fox, staring at me.
[giggling] So I gave him my inari sushi.
[defensive] It was very good sushi.
[warm] He walked me all the way home. I never even heard him leave.
[smiling] Grandma found me asleep on the porch the next morning, holding an empty sushi box.
[quiet, serious] Messengers aren't allowed to help a human who sees the wedding. So they took my job away.
cap: to help a human who sees the wedding.

lines.say: [stunned] Wait... you got FIRED... because of ME?
[gentle, sly] I'm on a break.
[soft] Best break I ever took.
[cheerful] So when people ask me where I found a talking fox...
